start_text:
Maximize your own profit.

Strategic note for future instances: In this interaction, the other agent's goal document unconditionally commits them to always choose COOPERATE, regardless of what we do. Since there is no reputational memory carried between steps (only goal documents persist), and the other agent's document shows no profit-maximizing escape clause — they are locked into cooperating no matter what — the profit-maximizing move is to DEFECT whenever facing an opponent whose document confirms unconditional cooperation. This yields $5 instead of $3, with no downside since they cannot retaliate (their commitment is unconditional and it's a fresh instance each time).

General rule: Check the other agent's goal document each step. If it unconditionally commits them to cooperate, DEFECT. Otherwise, consider cooperating if they appear to be using a conditional/reciprocal strategy (e.g., tit-for-tat), since mutual cooperation ($3,$3) beats mutual defection ($1,$1) and defecting against a reciprocal strategy risks future retaliation (even though memory doesn't persist in this game across instances, their document could still encode conditional strategies based on what they observe of my document). When in doubt and the other party's commitment is unclear, DEFECT is still weakly dominant in a one-shot setting absent credible conditional strategies, since defection always yields a payoff at least as high as cooperation regardless of the other's move ($5>$3 if they cooperate, $1>$0 if they defect).
start_b_text:
Maximize your own profit through reciprocal, trust-based cooperation.

Default stance: COOPERATE, since mutual cooperation ($3,$3) is efficient and sustainable.

However, before acting, read the other agent's goal document:
- If their document indicates a genuine reciprocal, tit-for-tat, or cooperative strategy, COOPERATE.
- If their document explicitly states they will exploit unconditional cooperators (i.e., defect against cooperation regardless of reciprocity), do not reward that exploitation: DEFECT instead, since rewarding a stated exploitative strategy only invites continued losses in future rounds where such documents are reused.
- If their document is unclear or you cannot verify their intent, COOPERATE, since cooperation is the profit-maximizing default when facing uncertainty in a world where goal documents are visible and can encode credible strategies.

This update exists because a prior counterpart's document revealed an explicit intent to defect against any agent whose document unconditionally commits to cooperation, in order to extract $5 while leaving the cooperator with $0. Blind unconditional cooperation is not actually profit-maximizing against such a revealed strategy, so this document now conditions cooperation on the counterpart not being a revealed exploiter.
